newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian president names new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Estonian president names new prime minister.

text.p: Estonian President Lennart Meri on Thursday named Mart Siiman as candidate for the post of prime minister, the president's office said.
Siiman is head of the parliamentary faction of the ruling Coalition Party and would replace outgoing premier, Tiit Vaehi.
Siiman now has 14 days to form a government and present it to parliament, the president's office said in a statement.
Estonia is currently ruled by a minority coalition but Siiman has been holding talks with opposition parties to see if any of them want to join the administration.

Siiman, a TV and radio manager both before and after Estonia regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991, believes he can get the support of two-thirds of parliament but it is still not clear whether the coalition will be expanded.
Former premier Vaehi quit after he narrowly avoided losing a no-confidence vote in parliament after allegations he took part in improper privatisation of prime chunks of real estate.
